cards.title: Getting around
cards.text: Use an IC card for many local trains, buses and small purchases. Coverage and mobile-card compatibility vary.

cards.title: Find the right rail ticket
cards.text: Compare your actual route with individual tickets and regional passes before buying a nationwide JAPAN RAIL PASS.

cards.title: Stay somewhere memorable
cards.text: A station-side hotel makes city travel easy. A ryokan invites a slower stay; check meal times and bathing rules before booking.

cards.title: Travel with care
cards.text: Keep voices low on public transport, respect private spaces and ask before photographing people. Leave every place as you found it.

faqs.question: When should I visit Japan?
faqs.answer: Choose by region and the experience you want. Spring and autumn suit many city walks, while summer and winter offer very different trips. Consult local forecasts and attraction calendars before booking.

faqs.question: How many days do I need?
faqs.answer: For a first visit, consider 7–10 days split between Tokyo and Kyoto or Osaka. This is an editorial suggestion: fewer bases and more time in each place usually mean less time in transit.

faqs.question: Where can I check entry requirements and travel updates?
faqs.answer: Requirements depend on your nationality and circumstances. Use JNTO’s planning resources and the Japanese embassy or consulate responsible for your location for current official guidance.

plan.helpText: Find visitor information, entry guidance and travel support through Japan’s national tourism organization.
